exposure: patients who underwent only cesarean section
cohort: 199 patients who either underwent a cesarean myomectomy (n=99) or a cesarean section alone (n=100) at a single center between December 2015 and September 2020
finding: Performing myomectomy during cesarean section increased the duration of operation, hospital stay, and amount transfused, but did not cause major complications and helped patients avoid a second surgery.
